problem: S3-STAB-01: The poll's condition `listings()` is a synchronous read of the fake volume's log: it copies the log, then filters every operation through `standardizedFileURL`, which is slow under TSan. The held-unit read comes after it, as a separate hop to the SteppedBlockingExecutor actor. Losing timeline, checked against SteppedBlockingExecutor.swift:30-46 and :60-62. (1) Round k: listings()==0, heldUnits.first==R (phase 4's root listing), release(R). release only resumes R's gate; R's work() runs later on the executor actor. (2) Round k+1 reads listings()==0, because R has not run yet. (3) R runs and records the root listing; the store resumes and submits phase 4's next listing U2, which is held. (4) Round k+1 then reads heldUnits==[U2] and releases it, so U2's listing runs. (5) Round k+2 sees listings()==2>0 and returns. requireHeldUnits(atLeast:1) now holds U3. (6) The stop (cancel or close) plus releaseAll runs U3, so listings()==3 and the `#expect(listings() == 2)` at :446 fails. The product is correct: in the replay, exactly one listing (the unit in flight) runs after the stop (`listings() == atStop + 1` holds). Only the test's oracle depends on the schedule. This reproduces the cycle-5 verifier's diagnosis in ADR-055 / L5K-R27 (2).

problem: S3-STAB-02: Each poll evaluates `if <condition> { return … }; if let unit = await executor.heldUnits.first { release(unit) }`. The condition is a synchronous read of the fake volume, or a hop to the store actor through `harness.record`/`state`. A round whose condition read predates the run of the unit released by the previous round, and whose `heldUnits` read follows that unit's run and the store's submission of its next unit, releases that next unit. That is the S3-STAB-01 timeline with a different condition. The unit released is the one the test means to hold. In chunkYieldRevalidates it is eviction's between-chunk yield, so y2 and y3 are evicted before the test reads y2 and leases y3. In chunkCountsRecords and in the tests at :553/:615 it is again the chunk yield, so firstChunk includes a second chunk. In evictionDuringReusingPublication it is the placement unit, so the publication ends and `requireHeldUnits` then waits out the time limit. In EvictionOverlapTests it is the first-chunk yield, so the plan no longer lists o2 and o3. In cancelledCollection(.stagingGC) it is the second removal: the third removal is submitted before the cancel, the collection removes all three files and returns success. In cancelDuringSecondRemoval it is the second removal unit, so `exists(second)` fails. In sweepChunksReleaseActor it is the sweep's chunk yield, so planted[1] is doomed. PurgeTests.untilPurgeReturnsOrWaits (:376-391) already reads `heldUnits` before its condition, which closes the window.

detail.fix: Apply the same transformation as S3-STAB-01 at every listed site: read `heldUnits` first, then the condition, and release only a unit read before a false condition. confirmer.reason: This is stronger than the hunter's evidence: two of the listed sites failed naturally in the unchanged originals, with exactly the predicted symptoms. (1) Debug, --repetitions 1000 over the 11 listed tests (load ~20-22): `EvictionTests.chunkYieldRevalidates` failed once. Issues: EvictionTests.swift:73 `isPresent(assets[2]…)`, :75 `location(for: y2) != nil`, and :50 `Caught error: .notPresent(y3)`. So y2 and y3 were evicted before the test read y2 and leased y3. (2) TSan, --repetitions 400 (load ~17-20): `EvictionOverlapTests.applyPlanAtChunkYield` failed twice at EvictionOverlapTests.swift:114 with `plan.victims → [o4, o5]` instead of `[o2, o3]`; 0 TSan reports. I read every listed site; each has the same shape: a condition read, then a separate hop for `heldUnits.first` or `heldUnits.isEmpty`, then a release. In IdempotencyTests.cancelledCollection the second half is `heldUnits.isEmpty` followed by `releaseNext()`, two separate hops, so the fix must release a unit read before the condition, not call releaseNext. I agree that :516-524 only changes which interleaving is covered. The fix (read held units before the condition) is sound by the same monotonicity argument as S3-STAB-01, because the store changes the state before it submits the next unit. I did not measure it here, since the rate is about 1 in 1,000-2,000. It is a flake under Q-5/Q-3, and the oracles hold only under one schedule (G4), so it is blocking. The files are under Tests/ZTronAssetStorageTests/Cleanup/**, owned by WP-C. A shared poll helper in Core/CoreHarness.swift would be outside WP-C's files; the per-site fix stays within them. problem: S3-STAB-04: These tests await `.task.value` (or `.result`) of unstructured tasks running product calls, with no prior cancellation-aware 'ended' wait. Swift Testing's time limit cancels only the test's own task, and cancellation does not reach the awaited unstructured task. If a product wait ever lost its resume, the test would record 'Time limit was exceeded' and the test process would never exit, so verify.sh would hang rather than report. closeResumesAWaitingAsker (:203-207) and closeWhileTheBatchWaits (:371-375) already use `CorePoll.until("…ended") { await LegacyRace.ended(...) }` first (L5K-R25). problem: S3-CRAS-02: OracleTests never calls runDueWork(), settleDeletions() or reapDeletable(). open(), close() and apply() never reap (checked). Evicted and removed blobs are therefore doomed but never unlinked in any lifetime: the 'evict' and 'remove' steps model only the index half, and no crash ever lands inside a deletion unit. The comment at line 204 says the doomed blob 'waits for a relaunch or the reaper', but neither ever comes. As a result the shipped oracle passes with every deletion-protocol mutant: C (reaper ignores the commit blocker), F (no acknowledged snapshot needed) and S (no grace). Those mutants are killed only by targeted unit tests (StoreDeletionTests, LeaseTests, StoreRecoveryTests), so the requirement is still covered elsewhere.
fix: The model-based oracle (`OracleTests`) must include deletion work (settle/reap) in its operation sequences so blobs are really unlinked, with I-3 asserted after every step; the confirmer's mutant Z (a `fatalError` in `BlobDeletionUnit.run`) must fail it.

confirmer.reason: Confirmed. OracleTests.swift contains 0 calls to runDueWork, settleDeletions or reapDeletable. In Sources, reap(maxKeys:) is reached only from performRunDueWork and from purge's reapDeletable. BlobDeletionUnit.run is the only blob unlink and is called only from reap. open() removes only foreign names. My mutant Z puts a fatalError in BlobDeletionUnit.run: the shipped OracleTests still passes all 16 seeds, so no blob is ever unlinked in its sequences. The reaping probe hits the fatalError, so it does unlink (2-7 unlinks per seed in the baseline, matching the hunter's log). I-3 therefore holds vacuously in the oracle. One limit of the proposed fix: my mutant G makes deletionBlocker return .none for every doomed key, so the reaper skips the ack, commit, lease and grace checks. It is NOT detected by the hunter's reaping oracle, by any S3AuditSink-audited probe, by StoreCrashTests or by CleanupCrashTests eviction. S3AuditSink.violations only checks paths in the current snapshot, despite its doc comment mentioning grace, and the sink acknowledges inline. So the fix needs the non-acknowledging sink and a grace-aware audit, not just a reap step. Non-blocking: I-3 is genuinely verified elsewhere. Under G, StoreDeletionTests and other targeted tests failed (8 failing tests, 29 issues). The oracle still checks I-1, I-2, I-4, I-5 and oracle agreement, so it is not assertion-free (G4). Dropping the reap was recorded with ruling R3 (c.md:975), though that record did not note the I-3 vacuity. Owner C (Cleanup/OracleTests.swift). Evidence: confirm-crash/S3-CRAS-02-confirm-run.txt and S3-CRAS-02-03-confirm-mutants.diff.

problem: S3-B-036: Legacy migration on a device: the Caches to Application Support rename on one APFS volume, a root on another volume, LiveLegacyDefaults, Unicode normalisation or case differences between legacy path components and disk names, the overlap guard's identity walks and sandbox stat refusals (/var to /private/var, App Group containers), and phase 3's ordered vs durable commit (OI-2)
fix: Record. S3-B-026 (OI-4): within C2 at 10,000 (2.5 ms); the async contract change is declined for Stage 3. S3-B-027: liveness under continuous stamping; OPTIONAL fix only if C-24's serial fits inside WP-C's files. S3-B-035: audit by reading that every persisted WP-B write bumps `commits.mutationSerial` in its turn, and record the audit table. The NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW items stay as ratified.
